commits: 5acc20d3a54c0c502f5ef53dba6cc3707b48538d Add rules profiles and empty survival scenario
1.1.handover:
**What landed** — commit `5acc20d` adds an explicit `first-playable`/`survival`
rules profile behind the existing `game` facade. Omitted and explicit
first-playable construction, snapshots and field/observation outputs keep the
historical shape. Survival construction produces an empty world with no fixed
sites, rejects legacy fixed-site scenario data, and snapshots carry
`rules: "survival"` for round-trip. The browser reads `?rules=`, keeps
first-playable by default, and exposes `data-rules`; a small browser suite covers
both selections. `docs/survival-coverage.md` maps §2 as implemented and §§3–8 as
pending with owners. README/AGENTS/direction now say the pass is started.

**Landmark drift** — no source drift. The only interface change is
`initial(options?: unknown)`; `initial()` still works and snapshots of
first-playable worlds still omit `rules`.

**Deviations from the work order** — survival snapshots emit `buildings: []`,
and the parser accepts an empty survival buildings array but rejects any entry;
this keeps snapshot round-trip natural without admitting fixed sites. Survival
mode keeps the existing BASE terrain and no-ops the legacy fixed-site
`build`/`link`/`preview` paths, since terrain and input are later units. Added a
browser profile-selection test in addition to the required core tests.

**What the next session must know** — current internal rules guards live in
`compose`, `impsOf`, `build`, `link`, `siteAt`, `preview` and `observe`.
`game.snapshot` is the source of the browser's `data-rules`. Survival still uses
the legacy economy tick over an empty buildings map; unit 1.2 must replace the
survival fixed-site rejection and add dynamic buildings/IDs before extending
snapshots. Historical browser tests still omit `?rules=`; add
`?rules=first-playable` only when unit 2.3 makes survival the default. Full

browser tests, coverage and contract checks, typecheck, benchpress lint).

to first-playable in the browser; core constructors reject them. No terrain,
typed input, finder or combat behavior is implemented or claimed.

commits: fe5fd4dddc866186e49bc74f1f99ecad430e1b2c Add dynamic survival buildings and the fixed gate
1.2.handover:
**What landed** — commit `fe5fd4d` adds survival dynamic building identity and placement. `game.place(world, center, kind)` centres an 11x7 footprint on the cursor, rejects out-of-interior, gate-reserved, overlapping and above-cap placements atomically, and allocates the first free `b001`..`b032` ID only on success. Survival scenarios/snapshots now carry `{ id, kind, center, mana?, link?, produced? }` entries and a `rally` (default `(13,10)`); observations expose `buildings`, `rally`, dynamic `siteAt`/`siteAtCursor`, links and pending sources. The fixed gate renders `/O\`, `|O|`, `\O/` at `(200,136)` with its `x=198..202, y=134..138` reservation honoured by placement and composition. `tests/core/survival-buildings.test.ts` covers edges, overlap, scenery clearing, gate exclusion, ID sequencing, the 32 cap, arbitrary links, rejected scenarios and snapshot round-trip. Coverage and AGENTS reflect the new state.

**Landmark drift** — `SiteDefinition` remains the fixed-site type; dynamic placements live in a separate internal `dynamic: Map<id, center>` alongside the shared buildings map. `Well.link` and `pendingSource`/`insertSite`/`siteAt` are widened from `SiteId` to `BuildingId`; legacy runtime validation is unchanged. `Observation.sites` remains the historical fixed-site map.

**Deviations from the work order** — the survival footprint operation is exported as `game.place` rather than overloading legacy `game.build`, so fixed-site construction stays exactly intact. Dynamic scenario entries use `center` (the captured cursor) rather than top-left coordinates. Placement uses the first unused ID instead of max+1, which still produces b001..b032 in successful construction order from an empty world and avoids filling scenario gaps. `game.link` is shared across profiles with per-profile ID validation. The web inspector now reads dynamic buildings from `observation.buildings` so survival scenarios do not show a false "empty" label.

**What the next session must know** — 2.2 should build on `game.place` and `place`'s validation helpers (`insideInterior`, `overlapsGate`, `patch`, `overlaps`) when adding typed Insert, Name and rally commands. Dynamic economy is deliberately not wired into `advance`: the legacy tick still iterates `SITE_DEFINITIONS` only, so scenario-provided dynamic mana does not generate/transfer yet (3.1). `compose` draws the gate only for survival, before dynamic buildings. `space f` on a survival dynamic building currently reports "No site at cursor" because the legacy Build menu only accepts fixed IDs; 2.2 replaces that path. Historical browser default is still first-playable; keep `?rules=first-playable` migration for 2.3.

**Open problems** — none blocking. Dynamic buildings are core/scenario-only until 2.2; no names, finder, troop motion, waves or combat exist. `direnv exec . just verify` and `direnv exec . just test` both pass at HEAD (231 core tests, 72 browser tests, coverage/contract checks, typecheck, benchpress lint).

commits: 79c5ccdebf07829668e68109f9a1ce272c99e969 Add typed survival construction, names and rally commands
2.2.handover:
**What landed** — commit `79c5ccd` replaces survival's Build path with typed Insert, names, connected and the shared rally command. In survival, Normal `i` opens Insert on any cell, captures the cursor cell and any footprint building, lists ordered candidates, completes with Tab, commits only on Enter, and creates a cursor-centred dynamic building through the existing placement rules. Successful builds open name editing; empty/Escape/blur/hidden retain the default `Well b001`/`Ring b002`, Enter trims a custom name. Names persist through observations and snapshots. Exact `rally` stores the captured cell, renders a flag marker and HUD coordinates; invalid/cancelled commands leave the point alone. The browser now shows Insert candidates and the live Name prompt, and prevents Tab/Enter defaults only while it handles them. Legacy Build, `connect`+Escape staging and the first-playable browser default remain unchanged.

**Landmark drift** — `InsertMode` now allows a null captured building and lives beside a new `NameMode` in `src/core/world.ts`. Placement was factored into a private `placeSurvival` result helper; public `game.place` keeps its identity-on-failure contract. `Well`/`Ring` gained an optional `name`; survival `BuildingObservation`, `SurvivalBuildingSetup` and snapshots expose a required name. Observation gained `insertCell`, `nameTarget` and `candidates`. HUD gained `#hud-rally`; render gained `drawRally` and survival datasets `insertCell`, `nameTarget`, `candidates`, `rally`.

**Deviations from the work order** — exact commands are recognised even when not among the visible candidates, so typing a building command on a footprint reaches placement and reports the specific overlap instead of only "unknown command". `rally` invalid input returns Normal with a notice while leaving the rally cell and source untouched. Scenario names are validated but kept verbatim when nonblank; only the Name prompt trims. Browser survival tests live in a new `tests/browser/survival-construction.spec.ts` rather than changing legacy suites, preserving their default-profile routing.

**What the next session must know** — Survival is still opt-in and the browser still defaults to first-playable until 2.3. `observation.candidates` is filtered by the current draft only in Insert; `commandCandidates` still exposes the full ordered list internally. Name editing starts after the default name is already assigned, which is what makes Escape/blur non-destructive. `placeSurvival` still checks `impsOf`, which returns no survival imps yet; 3.x must ensure living imps are visible there. `game.snapshot` does not carry an active Insert/Name draft, matching prior snapshot behavior. Dynamic economy remain unwired.

**Open problems** — none blocking. Finder, troop motion, waves and combat are absent as planned. `direnv exec . just verify` and `direnv exec . just test` pass at HEAD (248 core tests, 90 browser tests).

commits: 52c9ce11edc161033121bb9922496ba2731e1ae5 Add survival building finder and default browser play
2.3.handover:
**What landed** — commit `52c9ce1` adds the survival building finder and makes survival the browser default. Normal Space `f` opens Finder with an empty query, lists built buildings plus `Rally | rally | rally` and `Enemy gate | spawn | gate`, and matches an ASCII-case-insensitive subsequence of `name type ID`. Up/Down clamp, query edits reset selection, Enter jumps to the selected building centre, rally cell or gate centre, no-result Enter stays open with a notice, and Escape closes without moving. Jumps preserve a staged well source, so `i connect Enter` still links after navigating. The browser renders a readable finder panel and HUD entries, handles real arrow/Enter keys, and ignores navigation bindings while Finder is open. Survival's normal and finder cursor displacements now share one sweep helper, ready for enemy collision. Historical browser suites explicitly request `?rules=first-playable`; default page load is survival.

**Landmark drift** — Finder types and helpers added beside Insert/Name in `src/core/world.ts`; `leaderStep` branches to Finder for survival. `Observation` gained `finder: { query, selection, entries } | null`; `FinderEntry`, `FinderObservation` are exported through `src/core/game.ts`. `survivalDisplacement` lives near the mode steps and is used by both finder Enter and ordinary survival navigation. `src/web/main.ts` flips the default profile, adds `drawFinder`, finder HUD text and datasets. All historical browser suites now route explicitly through `?rules=first-playable`.

**Deviations from the work order** — Escape from Finder preserves a staged source; only blur/hidden clear it, following §5's explicit separation. The shared displacement sweep is applied to all survival cursor movement now, not just finder jumps, so §7 has one entry point already. A rules query other than `first-playable` (including absent or invalid) selects survival. The finder panel scrolls its visible window around the selection when entries exceed the viewport; selection still spans all entries.

**What the next session must know** — `hostileAt` inside `survivalDisplacement` currently delegates to `impsOf`, which still returns no survival imps; §6/§7 must feed living hostile troops (with factions) into it. The blocked-jump branch already closes Finder at the last safe cell with a `Blocked by hostile at x,y` notice but is untested because enemies do not exist yet. `finderOrigin` is captured and reset but not otherwise consumed; `game.snapshot` does not retain an active Finder, matching Insert/Name behavior. Finder sorts special destinations among buildings by name, so `Enemy gate` precedes `Foo` and `Rally` follows it. `just verify` and `just test` pass at HEAD (258 core tests, 100 browser tests).

**Open problems** — None blocking. Blocked finder movement and hostile notices await the troop state. Combat, waves, death and the remaining §7/§8 UI are still absent as planned.

commits: f185dfe75f2107bbf0c26f77c8e79817381d05d3 Add living survival troops and simultaneous combat
3.1.handover:
**What landed** — commit `f185dfe` adds living survival troops, validated troop
scenarios/snapshots, replacement production and simultaneous combat. Survival
troops carry stable IDs, faction, origin ring/serial, position, HP and
`nextAttackTick`. Allies use `ring#serial` IDs (`b001#1`, ...); enemies use a
validated explicit ID that cannot take the allied form. Observation/snapshot add
`troops`, `cursorHp`, `kills`, and survival rings expose total `produced` plus
`living`. Exported tuning constants are `ALLY_HP`, `ENEMY_HP`, `CURSOR_MAX_HP`
and `ATTACK_COOLDOWN`. Survival economy now walks dynamic IDs (the old code only
walked fixed sites): generate, transfer in ID order, then summon. A ring with
1000 mana and fewer than five living allies spends 1000 at its first patch-row-6
exit free of troops/cursor and allocates the next serial; all-blocked spends
nothing. Combat uses a pre-damage snapshot: each ready troop selects one adjacent
opponent by lowest HP then lexical ID, enemies prefer adjacent allies before the
cursor, all damage applies together (mutual kills), dead troops are removed, and
only actual attackers set `nextAttackTick=tick+10`. Newborns get `tick+10`.
Tests cover production exits/replacements, damaged troops, origin-ring counts,
cooldowns, lowest-HP/ID selection, mutual kills, cursor damage, pause/partition
determinism, snapshot round-trip and rejected setup.

**Landmark drift** — `generate`/`transfer`/`summon` became ordered helpers, with
`tickWorld` owning per-tick state and `summonSurvival`/`combatPhase` beside it.
`impsOf` still returns legacy ordered slot imps only, as required. `placeSurvival`
now checks `state.troops` instead of `impsOf` when blocking footprints.

**Deviations from the work order** — I implemented cursor damage during the
combat tick phase (authority §6, enemies choose allies before cursor) but not the
§7 HP-0 game-over/restart boundary, which remains unit 3.2. Consequently
`cursorHp` can reach 0 without freezing or restarting in this unit. Survival
wells now generate/transfer because production needs a funded ring; the browser
construction test's expected well mana changed from 0 to two ticks of
`WELL_GENERATION`, recorded in survival coverage. Survival ring `produced` is now
an unbounded safe integer (total serials) while legacy rings keep the five cap.

**What the next session must know** — Troops live in `state.troops` as a
discriminated union; combat sorts by ID, but `snapshot` also sorts troops for a
stable shape. Scenario allies must set `serial <= ring.produced`; enemies cannot
use `ring#serial` IDs to avoid future spawn collisions. `survivalDisplacement`
still calls `impsOf`, so cursor collision remains unwired exactly as the unit
requires. Field composition draws all survival troops as `i` after buildings.
`game.observe` keeps `impCount`/`imps` historical, so survival population is read
from `troops` and ring `living`. The `main.ts` survival ring HUD now shows
living/total. Existing survival scenarios with ring `produced` still round-trip;
the added `living` field is observation-only and is not in snapshots.

**Open problems** — None blocking. §7 waves, hostile/allied movement, cursor
collision, game over and restart are still absent by design. Dead-ally population
replacement is tested; enemy waves must reuse these cooldown/combat rules rather
than adding a second combat path.

commits: bb0717b44b62dee1ddf6370ea3662ff311a5c262 Add survival waves, hostile chase and cursor death
3.2.handover:
**What landed** — commit `bb0717b` adds fixed-gate survival waves, hostile chasing, cursor collision, game over and restart. Waves start at tick 300 and every 200 ticks, with size `min(n+2,16)`, spawning the first free cells of the gate's 16-cell Chebyshev-radius-2 perimeter up to the 128-enemy cap. Enemies move every fifth tick in lexical ID order over one BFS field from the cursor, holding when adjacent to an ally or the cursor, with earlier moves already counted as occupancy. Cursor displacement (normal, find, line, word and finder) now sees living hostile troops: the first hostile sample or diagonal side cell stops at the last safe sample, deals 1 if its cooldown is ready, and sets `nextAttackTick=elapsedTicks+10`. HP 0 clears mode/source/drafts, drops the remainder, ignores later play, and unblocked Enter restarts a fresh survival world. Browser restart resets the clock anchor. Observations add `gameOver`, `wave` and `nextWaveTick`; exports add `ENEMY_CAP`, `WAVE_START_TICK`, `WAVE_INTERVAL`, `WAVE_MAX_SIZE`.

**Landmark drift** — `tickWorld` now runs economy, `spawnWave`, `moveHostiles` on movement ticks, `combatPhase`, then terminal handling. New helpers sit beside `combatPhase`: `MOVE_OFFSETS`, `distanceField`, `moveHostiles`, `GATE_PERIMETER`, `waveAt`, `waveState`, `spawnWave`, `isGameOver`, `terminal`. `hostileAt` now returns the first enemy troop instead of consulting legacy `impsOf`; `moveCursor`/`contact` wrap the existing sweep. `dispatch` handles blur/visibility first, then blocks all non-restart events while game over. `place`/`link` now also refuse a dead world.

**Deviations from the work order** — Distance fields and hostile steps cover all in-bounds cells, not strictly `x=1..238,y=1..158`, so a cursor standing on the `#` border stays chaseable; placements and wave spawns still use interior cells only. `wave`/`nextWaveTick` are derived from `elapsedTicks` rather than stored, so constructing a scenario at a wave tick reports that wave without retroactively spawning it. Wave IDs are `e<wave>-<ordinal>`; an existing scenario troop with a colliding ID makes spawning skip that ordinal. The wave spawn remains a live-prefix slice, so occupied/blocked perimeter cells make later available cells spawn earlier. `main.ts` only gains game-over clock text and datasets; the full HP/wave HUD remains unit 4.1.

**What the next session must know** — Allies are still stationary; only `moveHostiles` exists. `distanceField(sources)` is already multi-source and returns `-1` unreachable, so unit 3.3 can reuse it for rally, cursor and enemy fields without another BFS. Hostile movement selects the first unoccupied neighbour with strictly smaller distance in north/east/south/west order; congestion holds rather than routing around. Contact damage uses the current `elapsedTicks`, so repeated blocked input at one tick cannot stack; normal tick combat then resumes on the same enemy cooldown. Death also clears `notice` on blur/hidden; the core notice on death is `Game over — Enter restart`. `snapshot`/`scenario` have no new fields: game over is `cursorHp===0` and wave state is computed from `elapsedTicks`; a dead snapshot round-trips game state but not the transient notice. `just verify` and `just test` pass at HEAD: 278 core tests and 104 browser tests.

**Open problems** — Allied movement, rally-directed movement, aggro-return and the shared multi-source movement phase remain for 3.3. The HUD still lacks full HP/wave/enemy-population presentation and explicit non-color faction markers; that is 4.1.

commits: 27a97527b40fbf2f8761b8d82da95f87855535b0 Move allies to the rally and intercept enemies
3.3.handover:
**What landed** — commit `27a9752` adds the shared-rally allied movement phase.
Every fifth tick allies move before enemies over at most three shared BFS fields
(rally, cursor, all enemies). An ally uses the enemy field when its nearest
enemy is within `ALLY_AGGRO_RADIUS` (6) path cells, otherwise the rally field;
it takes the first unoccupied strictly-closer cardinal neighbour in
north/east/south/west order. Allies hold at distance zero, beside an opponent,
at a blocked approach and never enter the cursor cell. Earlier ally moves count
as occupancy for later allies and for hostile movement. Newborn allies obey the
current rally from their first movement phase. `ALLY_AGGRO_RADIUS` is exported
through `game.ts`.

**Landmark drift** — `distanceField` and `MOVE_OFFSETS` were already reusable.
`tickWorld` now runs `moveAllies` immediately before `moveHostiles` on movement
ticks. The new helper sits between `distanceField` and `moveHostiles`. The web
rally marker, HUD coordinates and finder destination already observed
`observation.rally`, so no web code changed.

**Deviations from the work order** — None in behaviour. I added
`tests/core/survival-allies.test.ts` rather than extending the wave/combat
suites, and also corrected the pending-allied-movement statements in `AGENTS.md`,
`README.md`, `docs/direction.md` and `docs/survival-coverage.md`. The gate
suppression/backlog check uses wave 14 with one occupied perimeter cell: it
spawns 15, and wave 15 fills 16 new `e15-*` IDs with no deferred `e14-16`.

**What the next session must know** — “Stable order” is lexical troop ID, so
`b001#10` sorts before `b001#2`; `snapshot` forces the same order. Ally hold
checks use enemy positions before the enemy movement phase, which is correct
because combat follows both movement phases. Enemy movement now sees allies at
their post-move cells, including any ally that moved adjacent to an enemy.
`ALLY_AGGRO_RADIUS` is a tuning export; tests read it rather than hard-coding 6
inside the boundary assertions. `just verify` passed after the commit: 289 core
tests and 104 browser tests, plus fixture/contract/typecheck/benchpress checks.

**Open problems** — Authority §4 still says a rally commit must reject a cell
occupied by an enemy, but `rallyProblem` only checks interior and the gate
reservation. That gap predates this unit and is untouched here. Full faction
colours, HP/wave/population HUD and the final end-to-end browser loop remain
unit 4.1. The workbench topic still describes the pre-survival state; it is
scheduled for removal in 4.1.

commits: 2fd3045e529cb23c766214242ae2addb287e5eb7 Render survival factions, health and status
4.1.handover:

Survival troops now render as cyan allies and orange enemies with distinct non-color markers (ally underline, enemy pip), damaged troops get health bars, and the HUD exposes cursor/nearby HP, wave and next-wave countdown, kills, and living allies/enemies. A game-over panel shows the restart key, and the browser datasets add `allies`/`enemies`. A deterministic real-key browser flow builds and names both buildings at chosen positions, links them, sets the rally beside the gate, produces and moves allies, fights a wave without dying, then dies and restarts; it runs in development and production. The authority moved to `docs/cursor-survival.md`, the coverage map has no pending rows, and the resolved workbench topic was removed with `benchpress rm`.

**Landmark drift** — `src/web/main.ts` retains `render` and gains `drawTroopMarkers`, `drawGameOver`, `nearbyHealth` and `waveLabel`. HUD markup gained `#hud-hp`, `#hud-wave`, `#hud-kills` and `#hud-pop`. The old authority path `docs/plans/CURSOR_SURVIVAL.md` is now `docs/cursor-survival.md`; execution front matter/context, AGENTS, README, direction and coverage point there. `docs/workbench/NEXT.md` was already empty and is unchanged.

**Deviations from the work order** — presentation is survival-only; first-playable rendering is unchanged. The new end-to-end suite is `tests/browser/survival-complete-loop.spec.ts` rather than a rewrite of the historical `complete-loop.spec.ts`, so the frozen first-playable loop stays intact. Exact tick checkpoints in the new flow (50, 5, 495, 100, 200) are deterministic consequences of the current tuning, not new constants.

**What the next session must know** — `just verify` passed after the commit: 289 core tests, 106 browser tests, fixture/contract/typecheck/benchpress checks. Colors live in the `colors` object in `src/web/main.ts`: ally `#5ad2c4`, enemy `#e47a52`, health background `#313b34`, overlay panel `#2a1716`. Grass and gate glyphs are antialiased, so pixel tests use tolerance for them; faction fill rects and health bars are exact. The complete-loop test deliberately moves the cursor off the rally cell before asserting the rally marker, because the gold cursor block otherwise covers the flag. The authority file body was left substantively unchanged; only its title/status line and path moved.

That gap predates this unit and is untouched. The execution plan and its `.state.json` were deliberately not edited; Ploopy closes them.
